title: Replacement Value of a Locked Gift Cards & Store Credit Card
content:
**Accounting clause.** The replacement value of a locked Gift Cards & Store Credit card starts from the protected balance, which is the sum of every entry on the locked card's ledger: the whole balance at the lock plus refunds received while locked, after any charge captured since the lock for an order placed before it. The investigation hold share is nothing, and the investigation hold is the protected balance times the investigation hold share, rounded half up to the cent. The replacement value is the protected balance less the investigation hold, in US dollars to the cent.

## Building the protected balance

| Entry on the locked card's ledger | Enters the protected balance |
|---|---|
| Loads and spending up to the lock (together, the whole balance at the lock) | Yes |
| Refunds received while the card is locked | Yes, added |
| A charge captured after the lock for an order placed before the lock | Yes, taken off |

## Worked figures (hypothetical locked card)

| Ledger entry | Amount (USD) |
|---|---|
| Initial load | 100.00 |
| Spent on an order before the lock | less 35.20 |
| Balance at the lock | 64.80 |
| Refund received while locked | plus 12.00 |
| Charge captured after the lock for an order placed before it | less 6.80 |
| Protected balance (sum of every entry) | 70.00 |
| Investigation hold (70.00 times a share of nothing) | 0.00 |
| Replacement value | 70.00 |

## Points of judgement

- **Spending before the lock** is part of the ledger and so already outside the protected balance.
- **A refund that arrives while the card is locked** belongs to the protected balance.
- **The figure is read from the ledger**, not from the customer's account of what the card held.
